That's first weird.
So your climate change program, the mass mobilization,
it's mandatory enrollment from the age of 18 to 26 to one year?
No, no. What I did say, I've not said mandatory enrollment,
but what I've said is this.
I would not submit legislation.
But what I have said is that I think it would be a very good idea to have a non-binding referendum,
a referendum that would only be votes taken among American citizens
between the age of 18 and 26.
I want to hear what Americans between 18 and 26 have to say about this.
So much of what I said tonight, entitled,
entails a huge shift, a huge season of moral repair.
Everything from our schools, to rural hospitals that are closing,
to the need for infrastructure repair,
for the re-greening of our economy, for the re-greening of our infrastructure,
the re-greening of our power rent,
this goes beyond even what the Green New Deal itself will do.
So what I have suggested is a referendum where people between the age of 18 and 26 will vote.
And I think at the very least this will be a very healthy conversation in our society.
And what I'd like to propose, if this referendum, the idea of this referendum,
the yes and the no, the yes would be one year of mandatory national service
for Americans between the age of 18 and 26.
At one point you would give one year to your country.
If you want to be a teacher, great,
because we really need you in one of these underserved schools.
You want to be a doctor or a nurse, great.
We really want to, we need you in these rural hospitals that are closing as we speak.
You want to be an architect, we really, really need you in order to,
in order to repair a bridge or hospital or whatever.
So that's the idea, only of a referendum, not a mandatory, nothing mandatory, just a referendum.
Thank you.
Ms. Williamson, you spoke at the No Labels Convention yesterday, and politics, 50, was there.
And that organization's goal is to work about compromising going across the aisle.
Obviously in the Senate, it's our public and majority, and it's very hyperpartisan.
How would you plan to get some of these plans passed, some of these, in the art of the compromise?
Well, obviously we have co-eval branches of government.
The President does not have a magic wand, which right now, thank God.
If you have a Democratic President, which we all believe should be committed to having a Democratic President in 2020,
then that President will have to be dealing.
Hopefully with the Democratic Senate, we shouldn't just assume that it will be a Republican Senate.
Everybody talks about y'all, the deal, the world, what's the Senate? Maybe not.
Maybe not, and I know in my case, if the conscience of this country is changing up to a like-me President,
it's reasonable to assume the conscience of this country is changing up, and they go up in the Democratic Senate.
Look what happened in the last midterm.
So I don't think we should go around accepting that Mitch McConnell is going to be the next Senate leader.
He absolutely might love it. But if it is a Republican, one more hope, that it would be a Republican party,
then as we claimed it's sold, because both major political parties need to do that right now,
there would be more statesmen who would actually be willing to work in an honorable way with the President.

where Mitch McConnell would be saying something along the line, what he said about Obama,
our biggest goal is that Obama will be a one-term President. Then not as President,
